Alex Kim: Heads up — RFC follow-up: proposing centralizing quantization/kernel selection into an 'inference-compiler' component. Want tradeoffs + rollout plan here.
Mira Chen: Short summary of benefits?
Alex Kim: Benefits: 1) single source of kernel heuristics and quantization profiles; 2) reuse compiled artifacts across runtimes -> faster cold-starts; 3) easier A/B of kernel improvements; 4) centralized telemetry for regressions.
Sam Patel: Concern: centralization increases blast radius — a bad compiler change could regress many models. Mitigation ideas?
Jordan Lee: Also network hop/latency if this becomes a remote service. We need to weigh in-process vs sidecar vs remote.
Alex Kim: Agreed. High-level options:
- In-process library (compilerlib): lowest latency, easiest for Private installs, but less isolation.
- Local sidecar RPC (co-located): isolates crashes, can be scaled independently, slight hop ~0.2-1ms.
- Remote service (cluster endpoint): strongest reuse but adds multi-ms hop, harder for on-prem.
Mira Chen: Prefer incremental: start as opt-in in-process lib used by a small subset, then extract to sidecar if we need isolation or scale. Keeps Private-friendly.
Sam Patel: For mitigation: strong regression gates, staged rollout, automatic fallback to previous kernel and per-model kill-switches. Perf harness must catch p95 regressions and correctness diffs.
Alex Kim: Proposed migration steps:
1) Define stable compilerlib API (C ABI + thin Rust/Go shims).
2) Implement compilerlib and a feature-flag path in runtime (opt-in). Put config behind 'inference.compiler.mode'.
3) Run full perf + LLM-output diff harness against model-suite A and B for 2 weeks.
4) Canary to internal traffic (5%) with circuit breakers & tracing enabled.
5) If stable, introduce sidecar as alpha, run 10% traffic, test autoscale behaviour.
6) For Private customers, deliver compilerlib build or local sidecar package; default to in-process if sidecar blocked.
InfraBot: perf-harness job 442 queued for model-suite-A run; ETA ~24h :rocket:
Jordan Lee: We should ensure Dedicated nodes can pin compiler version per pool. Also ensure rollback agent can flip models back to previous kernels without redeploy.
Sam Patel: Testing checklist additions: p50/p95/p99 token latency, cold-start latency, unit-cost delta, and an automated output-diff with thresholds per model. Add opt-in telemetry per token to avoid PII.
Mira Chen: Add an API compatibility test matrix (runtime versions x compilerlib ABI). Also add a migration guide for infra & on-prem ops.
Alex Kim: I will draft a migration RFC and checklist. Tentative timeline: 6 weeks to reach an opt-in in-process lib, 8–12 weeks to have sidecar alpha. Will call out owners and required perf sign-offs.
Jordan Lee: lgtm. Owners: @Alex Kim, @Sam Patel, @Mira Chen. I'll add tasks to the architecture board and schedule a follow-up sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
Alex Kim: Thanks — opening the PR for the API doc today. Will tag you all.
Sam Patel: Thanks — happy to own the regression harness integration.
Mira Chen: I'll own compatibility testing for Private/Dedicated.
InfraBot: ticket INF-312 created for 'inference-compiler migration' and linked to the RFC.
